answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity earn a jade credential through a narrowing canyon of sequential service: a newcomer must complete a chain of real tasks for distinct established peers, each task harder than the last, with a falcon-swift audit of the previous step before the next one unlocks. Because the chain is strictly sequential, an attacker cannot run a thousand fake identities in parallel; each extra identity costs a full fresh chain of real work, and bought credentials fail since each jade token is bound to the work history that produced it.
